# `¿` — Roll / Deal

Function. Keys: `Alt-/`. Ranks: `0` monadic, `0 0` dyadic

`¿N`: uniform draw from `⍳N`. `¿0`: U(0,1). Pervasive.

```bpl
¿6 ∊ ⍳6           ⍝ $t
```

`M¿N`: `M` draws without replacement from `⍳N`.

```bpl
≢3¿10             ⍝ 3ₓ
≢∪3¿10            ⍝ 3ₓ
```

Bounds are nonnegative integers; `M≤N`. Exact arguments give exact integer draws. Dyalog APL writes Roll and Deal as `?`, which BPL uses for [predicates](question.qmd).

`¿` draws from the session's stream of random numbers, which the operating system seeds when the session starts. [`•prefs ["seed":n]`](../system/prefs.qmd) seeds it with the nonnegative integer `n`, and the same seed gives the same draws. In a [map](../terms.qmd#term-map), each cell draws from a stream of its own. A cell's draws don't depend on how many values the other cells draw, or on whether the map makes a [batched call](../evaluation.qmd#functions-and-effects). [`•rand`](../system/rand.qmd) makes a separate stream.

```bpl
•prefs ["seed":42] ⋄ a←¿6 6 6 ⋄ •prefs ["seed":42] ⋄ a≡¿6 6 6    ⍝ $t
```
